lines.vo: At its narrowest the Strait of Hormuz is twenty-one miles across.
lines.image: a narrow sea channel between two arid headlands, seen from the air

lines.vo: The shipping lanes inside it are two miles wide. One lane in, one lane out.
lines.image: two tanker wakes running opposite ways in dark water

lines.vo: About twenty million barrels of crude oil pass through that gap every single day.
lines.image: a loaded crude tanker low in the water

lines.vo: That is close to a fifth of everything the world burns.
There is no way around it. The Gulf has one door, and this is the door.
lines.image: a rocky headland closing on a channel

lines.vo: Iran holds the northern shore. Oman holds the south. The outbound lane runs through Omani water.
lines.image: bare mountains falling straight into the sea

lines.vo: One tanker aground in a two-mile lane closes the strait for weeks.
lines.image: a grounded ship listing in shallow water

lines.vo: Every fuel price on earth moves when a warship changes course here.
lines.image: a warship bow wave in grey sea

lines.vo: Twenty-one miles of water, and there is no substitute for any of it.
lines.image: an empty grey sea at first light
lines.title: TWENTY-ONE MILES
